forms_signatures.text: ollows: B.2 STATEMENT OF WORK (SOW) 1. Contract Title: Surgical Instrument Repair Service 2. Background: Surgical Processing Service continues to require an on-site instrument repair/maintenance service. 3. Scope. The Gulf Coast Veterans Health Care System (GCVHCS), Biloxi, MS, requires a Contractor to provide monthly on-site same day services, to repair, refurbish, and assess for replacement, surgical instrument for use in operating room procedures, for rigid sterilization containers, and for case carts used for instrument transport at the GCVHCS, Biloxi MS and Joint Ambulatory Care Center, Pensacola FL. Preventive Maintenance (PM), scheduled repairs, refurbishment and assessment for replacement shall include but is not limited to all specialty trays by service (Ortho, ENT, etc.) scissors, osteotomes, curettes, periosteal elevators, gouges, knives to include sizes from micro to amputation, rongeurs, bone cutters, pin cutters, burrs, drill bits, all surgical forceps/clamps, all retractors, and all needle holders to include insert replacement. Contractor shall track refurbishing history by set to determine service schedule rotation. The Contractor shall provide repair service, which may consist of calibrating, cleaning, stain removal, lubricating, adjusting, replacing parts, and maintaining the equipment, insulation electrical safety inspection, as required by instrument type, including all emergency calls necessary between regular repairs. Upon completion of repair, refurbishment, and testing of the submitted instruments, rigid sterilization containers and case carts, the contractor must return the equipment to the Sterile Processing Section (SPS). The accreditation process is a complex system of interrelated activities that ensures the VA maintains a constant state of regulatory readiness and a safe healthcare environment. These services shall support eight (8) medical facilities in establishing a continuous readiness program to achieve and maintain compliance with Joint Commission (JC) standards. This includes compliance with the JC Program, Physical Environment (PE), Life Safety (LS), and Emergency Management (EM) standards. Location of Work: All work shall be performed at the Coast Guard Academy, 15 Mohegan Dr, New London, CT 06320. Site Visit: Bidders are encouraged to visit the site to become familiar with existing conditions. Failure to do so will not relieve the successful bidder from furnishing all labor, materials, and equipment to satisfactorily complete performance of all required work. Bidders shall contact the primary TA to schedule a site visit. Hours of Work: All work shall be performed between the hours of 7:30 a.m. and 4:00 p.m. local time, Monday through Friday excluding Federal Holidays. Should the contractor desire to work outside these hours, the contractor shall submit a request to the primary TA no less than 48 hours in advance. Scheduling of Work: The contractor shall schedule all work with the TA. Contractor’s Use of Premises: The contractor will be working within an operational Coast Guard military installation. PURPOSE: The Government is seeking information for innovative, modular, and interoperable solutions that support child welfare technology modernization for title IV-E agencies at the state level. Through this RFI, ACF seeks input from vendors on standards – aligned technologies and services that can assist states, territories, and tribes in exploring, planning, implementing, and maintaining child welfare technology solutions. SUBMISSION INFORMATION: All responses with the knowledge and/or experience to provide information referenced in this RFI and Statement of Objectives (SOO) are invited to submit, in writing, sufficient information within the page limitation (see RFI Administration and Response section). Please submit one (1) solution per response with a maximum of three (3) responses per vendor organization. This limit applies across all submissions made by the vendor organization. If a vendor organization submits more than three solutions or services, only the first three submissions will be reviewed and considered. Nothing contained in this contract shall relieve the contractor from complying with applicable Federal, State and Local laws, codes, ordinances and regulations, including obtaining licenses and permits, giving notices and submitting reports, in connection with environmental standards. Two (2) types of cleanings are authorized under this contract: CCI Cleaning and INSURV Cleaning. (a) CCI Cleaning. When designated, CCI Cleaning shall be performed in strict compliance with the applicable Maintenance Requirement Cards (MRCs). The Contractor shall accomplish all tasks, procedures, and completion criteria identified in the referenced MRCs. (b) INSURV Cleaning. When designated, INSURV Cleaning shall be limited in scope to cleaning the Landing Craft Air Cushion (LCAC) for the removal of salt, sand, oil, water, and debris from all external (topside) areas and specified internal compartments, including the Port and Starboard cabins. No maintenance actions, inspections, or preservation tasks beyond those expressly stated in this paragraph are required under INSURV Cleaning. 5.1. LCAC Cleaning. 5.1.1. Associated systems include: potable water, sewer, contaminated water reclamation and LCAC rinse facility, 400 Hz power provided to the apron and hangars, 100-foot apron lighting and compound security lighting, emergency diesel power generation, low pressure compressed air, fire detection and suppression prevention, physical security and cyber systems. As a tenant command on the Marine Corps Base, Camp Pendleton, ACU 5 must work with and through the base facilities organization to schedule and conduct repairs, upgrades and any new construction, while working through many other challenging processes such as environmental impact studies. Given the uniqueness of the LCAC and the fact most Sailors involved in maintenance come from ships and only serve one tour of duty in the LCAC community, they lack familiarity with the craft and its systems. The learning curve for personnel is steep and makes all tasks related to maintenance challenging and time consuming. In addition to complex maintenance, the LCAC requires in-depth cleaning to prevent corrosion on its aluminum hull and components. Even when not operating on the water, LCACs, by virtue of being located on the coast, are subject to severe corrosion due to salt and sand intrusion. Corrosion damage on LCACs is the number one driver of Non-Mission Capable (NMC) status at ACU5 and causes thousands of hours of costly weld repairs each year. Deep cleaning to remove salt and sand is necessary to keep the craft operational. 1.3. Objective: The goal of this effort is to improve the readiness and performance of LCACs at ACU 5. General Requirements The Contractor shall inspect all weight handling equipment listed in Appendix C of this speciﬁcation. The inspection shall include all accessories generic to the piece of equipment. Equipment identiﬁed as requiring a rated load and unit proof test shall also have the tests performed in accordance with the applicable sections of the references identiﬁed previously. As 6 part of the annual inspection requirement, the Contractor shall conduct a full functional no-load operational test and a rated load test (up to 110% of equipment capacity). Load testing is an inseparable component of the annual inspection and shall be included in the unit price. No separate pricing or invoicing for load testing will be accepted. 6.2. The COR shall review the equipment with the unit and determined whether or not there is an operational need for it or if it is good enough condition to pass both an inspection and load test. After consultation with the unit, the COR shall notify the contractor if the newfound equipment needs to be added to the contract equipment list and if unfound equipment needs to be removed. 6.6. Re-inspection and Follow-on Load Tests If during any test or inspection deﬁned in this speciﬁcation, the equipment fails to meet the reference requirements, the Contractor shall re-inspect said equipment after the Coast Guard has accomplished repair. This re- inspection shall include operational and rated load tests as required and described in this speciﬁcation. Re-inspections shall be completed, within thirty (30) calendar days after notiﬁcation by the Coast Guard that the equipment is ready for re-inspection.
